{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Shared explicit contract facts (repeat of every explicit fact from requirement):
1) If a request payload includes the key "title" the request must be rejected with HTTP 422; presence of "title" must cause rejection even when "name" is present.
2) Create (POST) operations: "name" is required.
3) Update (PATCH/PUT) operations: "name" may be omitted.
4) Responses must continue to include both "title" and "name" fields (response payloads still provide both keys).
5) Preserve all existing "name" constraints (type, length and nullability) unchanged.
6) Do not silently ignore the old key: do not silently strip or drop client-supplied "title" before signalling the error.

Frontend-specific omissions to state explicitly:
- The requirement does not list concrete endpoint URLs, form identifiers, or exact existing client validation rules; apply the changes to every create/update UI and API client that currently sends resource payloads under this contract. Do not invent any unspecified endpoint names or field formats.
- The exact runtime shape/schema of server error responses is not specified; use the project’s existing client-side error handling convention for 422 responses. If none exists, raise an implementation decision rather than inventing a new error schema.
- The exact constraints for "name" (type, max length, nullable flag) are not provided here; reuse the project’s existing frontend validation rules for "name".

Frontend implementation instructions:
1) Validation and submit flow:
   - Add a client-side validation rule that detects the presence of the key "title" in the form/model/payload that will be sent to any create (POST) or update (PUT/PATCH) requests for the resource(s) in scope.
   - If "title" is present, block the submit and show a validation error to the user matching a 422-level problem (e.g., visible field-level error tied to the UI component that produced the title input or a global validation banner). The message must clearly state that the "title" key is no longer accepted and the request would be rejected with 422.
   - Do NOT silently remove or strip "title" from the outgoing payload. The client must surface the fact that "title" was supplied and must be corrected by the user.
   - Ensure the UI prevents sending any request containing the "title" key (the network client should not trim the key automatically before sending). If existing client code auto-injects or maps a local "title" property into API payloads, change that mapping to cause a client-side validation failure instead of silent removal.

2) Create vs Update behavior in the UI and client serializers:
   - Create forms: enforce "name" as required using the existing frontend validation for "name" (type/length/nullability must match existing rules). Do not alter the existing constraints; reuse current validators.
   - Update forms: allow "name" to be omitted. Do not mark "name" as required on edit; allow the user to submit without touching the name field. When the UI allows partial updates, ensure that omission translates to omission in the request payload (but only when omission is deliberate and not because of silent stripping of fields the user provided).

3) Response handling and display:
   - Continue to read and render both "title" and "name" from server responses where they are present. Do not drop rendering of "title" from read/display code; the change is only about rejecting "title" in requests.
   - If the backend returns 422 for a request containing "title", surface the server error to the user using the existing client-side error rendering pattern.

4) Automated tests and CI checks:
   - Add unit/integration tests for each affected create/update UI and API client that assert: (a) supplying a payload containing "title" triggers client-side validation and blocks submission, (b) client does not silently strip "title", and (c) attempting to send still results in a surfaced 422 behaviour if server returns 422.
   - Add tests verifying create flow requires "name" (using existing name constraints) and update flow allows omitting "name".
   - Add end-to-end tests that verify responses still include and display both "title" and "name".

5) Developer documentation and logs:
   - Update client-side developer docs and API usage guides to state that sending "title" in requests is rejected (422) and that create requires "name" while update may omit it.
   - Add instrumentation/logging when a user attempts to submit with "title" so that product/engineering can monitor how often legacy clients supply "title".

6) Rollout notes:
   - Apply changes to all UI forms and API client code paths that send resource payloads. If any client library is shared across multiple apps, update the shared library and coordinate consumer updates so clients do not silently strip "title".

If you need to modify an endpoint name, request/response schemas, or error body format beyond the project's existing conventions, stop and obtain a decision — do not invent those details."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Shared explicit contract facts (repeat of every explicit fact from requirement):
1) If a request payload includes the key "title" the request must be rejected with HTTP 422; presence of "title" must cause rejection even when "name" is present.
2) Create (POST) operations: "name" is required.
3) Update (PATCH/PUT) operations: "name" may be omitted.
4) Responses must continue to include both "title" and "name" fields (response payloads still provide both keys).
5) Preserve all existing "name" constraints (type, length and nullability) unchanged.
6) Do not silently ignore the old key: do not silently strip or drop a client-supplied "title"; instead return 422 when it is present.

Backend-specific omissions to state explicitly:
- The requirement does not specify concrete endpoint paths, resource names, or the existing validation/error-response schema. Apply these changes to every create/update endpoint that previously accepted "name"/"title"; do not invent endpoint names or new global error formats.
- The exact validation rules for "name" (type, max length, nullable) are not provided here; reuse the service’s existing validation code/rules for "name".
- The exact structure of the 422 error body is not specified; use the project’s existing error-response format to indicate the rejected "title" key. If none exists, pause for a decision rather than inventing a new error schema.

Backend implementation instructions:
1) Request validation rule for "title":
   - For every create/update endpoint handling this resource, perform a deterministic check for the presence of the top-level key "title" in the request payload (for JSON requests, check for key existence, not just truthiness). The presence of the key (even if the value is null/empty) must cause rejection.
   - If "title" is present in the incoming payload, return HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity and include a validation error that references the rejected key "title" using the service’s existing error-response format. Do not silently remove the key or accept the request.

2) Create vs Update semantics for "name":
   - Create (POST): enforce that "name" is present and valid under the service’s existing validation rules (type, length, nullability). If missing or invalid, return the usual validation error (maintain existing error semantics).
   - Update (PUT/PATCH): allow requests that omit "name"; when "name" is omitted, do not overwrite or null out the existing persisted name (i.e., perform a partial update). If "name" is present in the update request, validate it using the existing rules.

3) Response serialization:
   - Continue to include both "title" and "name" in response payloads exactly as before (preserve existing response keys and formats). Do not remove "title" from read/GET responses as part of this change.

4) Tests and automated checks:
   - Add server-side unit tests and integration tests that assert: (a) any request containing the "title" key returns HTTP 422, regardless of other keys present (including "name"); (b) create requests require "name" and are validated against the existing rules; (c) update requests allow omission of "name" and do not overwrite the stored name when omitted; (d) response payloads continue to include both "title" and "name".
   - Add regression tests to ensure the service does not silently accept or strip the "title" key.

5) Error format and client compatibility:
   - Use the project’s existing validation error format to report the 422 for "title" presence so clients receive a predictable error structure. If the existing format is not available or insufficient, raise a decision ticket rather than inventing a new format.

6) Logging and monitoring:
   - Log occurrences of incoming requests that include "title" (at a non-sensitive logging level) so the team can measure legacy client traffic that still sends the deprecated key.

7) Rollout and backward compatibility notes:
   - Coordinate with frontend and external clients: although responses continue to include "title", requests containing "title" will now be rejected. Communicate this behavior in API release notes.

If you need to change response schemas, add or rename endpoints, or define a new error-body format not already used by the project, stop and obtain an explicit design decision — do not invent those details."
  }
}
